spark.lede: At 13:56 on 31 August you opened a session with a structured brief: refactor the Rust codebase toward a written quality bar, one unit at a time, audit first, and wait for your approval before touching code.
spark.body:
The spark was shaped as a template: the task, the process, the quality bar, an example and a verification clause, each in its own tag. It opened: "Refactor this Rust codebase incrementally toward the quality bar below. Preserve observable behavior throughout." The process it laid out had five steps: audit the codebase and rank the findings, wait for approval, then refactor one finding at a time with the gate run after each unit; write characterization tests before touching uncovered code; flag and stop on any change to public API or observable behaviour; report rather than rewrite if a rewrite ever looked cheaper.

The quality bar came in two halves: what the machine enforces, fmt, clippy with pedantic warnings as errors, the test suite, and what judgment weighs, no unwrap outside tests, functions that do one thing, newtypes over call-site validation, borrowing over cloning, no speculative abstraction.

The record traces this text to no earlier Claude turn. It was the first typed turn of the session that built the branch, four minutes after the previous one closed.

steering.lede: Ten steers, three of them from the two sessions before the spark. The turns that changed course came late: a question about stopping, a switch to Dutch, and a pull request you first meant to open yourself.
steering.body:
The first three steers predate the spark, from two sessions the record matched by time window. At 13:36, near the end of one, you typed a single word, "merged", and the build turned to the project memory file. Seven minutes later, in a fresh session, you asked "what issues are still remaining from the review we did?" and sent Claude back to make sure: close in tasqx what was done, report what stayed open. Four minutes after that session ended came the spark.

For the next two hours and eighteen minutes the record holds no steer. Claude's commits ran from 14:27 to 16:11. Then Claude asked which of four behaviour-changing fixes should go ahead, and you answered with your own question: "Is this a good moment to stop? Can we pick up another time? Or is the codebase in a non working state?" Forty seconds later you switched to Dutch: "Hebben we eigenlijk een goede code coverage tests?"

After a dwell of ten minutes, "Ik commit en maak een pr". Twenty-six seconds and one interrupt later, "Maak pr". After a dwell of 27 minutes you sent Claude to "check out the comments by coderabbitai". The last two steers bracket the merge: "keep an eye out for ci" twenty-four seconds before it, "merged, push a new release" thirty-four seconds after.

judgment.lede: Three moments in thirteen minutes, all at the point where the approved queue had been delivered and the next step needed a decision from you.
judgment.body:
All three judgments fall after the last of the thirty-four commits Claude ran. At 16:14:11 Claude raised a question through AskUserQuestion, asking which of four behaviour-changing fixes in tier 6 should go ahead; you rejected the call. Three seconds later you interrupted the text Claude was writing in its place, the one that began with "Action needed" and reported the approved queue delivered. The turn you typed instead, fifty seconds after the interrupt, asked whether this was a good moment to stop.

The third came at 16:27:04. Claude was answering your coverage question in Dutch, with the line, region, function and branch percentages from the last green CI run on main already on screen. You cut it off. Twenty-three seconds later came "Maak pr".

The record holds no rejected edit and no file changed by hand between Claude's edits. Each overrule here was of a question or an explanation, not of code.

build.lede: Thirty-four commits Claude ran in an hour and forty-three minutes, then a thirty-fifth the record cannot place. Most of the added lines were moved, not written: a six-thousand-line lib.rs split into seven modules.
build.body:
The first commit landed at 14:27, thirty-one minutes after the spark: four prints that never met emit, and the panic a closed pipe made of them. Claude committed every few minutes after that, thirty-four times by 16:11, each run as a Bash call within seconds to a few minutes of its timestamp. The subjects trace the queue: a storage fault shipped as an empty list, clocks read twice, clones that borrowing could replace, nineteen schemas rebuilt per call, then from 16:00 the split of lib.rs, backend.rs first out of a six-thousand-line file, and two chores for what the split left behind.

The thirty-fifth commit, whose subject the pull request carries, is dated 17:55:52. The sessions hold no command that matches it; the record does not say who ran it.

Of 3,932 added lines, 1,347 were emitted by Claude through a tool and 2,331 were moved, lines that also appear among the removed ones. 254 have no origin the record can name: hand-written, formatter output, or a shell transformation Claude ran; a sample to inspect, not a tally of your typing. Iterations: 27 tool errors, 69 test-suite runs, 11 files edited more than twice, render.rs the most at 22.

ship.lede: Merged at 18:05:06 by GitHub. No merge command appears in the sessions; the nearest trace of you is a turn thirty-four seconds after: "merged, push a new release".
ship.body: The record of the ship is short. The merge is timed at 18:05:06 on 31 August and attributed to GitHub; the accountable human is the commit author, Dimitri Tholen, together with whoever pressed it. The sessions hold no attempt before the merge: no gh pr merge, no failed try, no fallback command. What they hold is the turn you typed twenty-four seconds before it, "keep an eye out for ci", and the one thirty-four seconds after, reporting the merge done and asking for a release. Between those two turns the pull request went from open to merged, with GitHub as the recorded merger and nothing in the transcript to show the press.

unseen.lede: Three hours and forty-eight minutes at the keyboard in one session, by the record's measure. What that time held between turns, the record cannot say.
unseen.body:
The record measures three hours and forty-eight minutes of presence in one session. It holds the turns you typed and the moment each one arrived; it holds nothing of what came before them.

The record holds no evidence of how you read the ranked findings the spark asked for, or of what you weighed in the pause between Claude's question about tier 6 and your question about stopping. It holds no evidence of what filled the dwell before you sent Claude to the coderabbitai comments, or the one before "Ik commit en maak een pr", or of what turned that into "Maak pr" half a minute later. It holds no evidence of who ran the thirty-fifth commit, or of anyone watching the CI run.

Reading, thinking and silent deciding leave no line in a transcript. The story tells what it can trace and names the rest as yours.
